newsitem.title: UK: Barclays shares drop in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Barclays shares drop in heavy trading.

text.p: Shares in Barclays Plc fell in heavy trading on Tuesday with dealers saying there were signs of switching out of the stock and into other leading bank shares.

Traders said some earnings estimates for Barclays were being trimmed slightly after 1996 pre-tax profits at the low end of expectations, but said the sharp fall in the shares largely reflected profit-taking after recent strong gains.

"They have had a good run and this is just like the day after the Lord Mayor's show," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage. "There is switching out of Barclays and into anything else in the sector."
He said Lloyds TSB Group Plc, up 4-1/2p at 523, was in favour for a second day since last week's results showed it to have better margins on its domestic business than Barclays.
Barclays was down 23p at 11.76-1/2 by 1126 GMT in heavy volume of 9.6 million shares, making it the second most active stock in the London market.

"The stock has had a good run and the results were just not good enough to push it any higher," said another dealer. "The results were a little disappointing and there was a lack of specific news on a share buyback."
Other bank stocks were mostly higher with HSBC Holdings Plc up 29-1/2p at 15.59 stg and Abbey National Plc up 6-1/2p at 791-1/2.

However National Westminster Bank Plc, also heavily exposed to the same investment banking field responsible for at least some of the shortfall at Barclays, where operating profits at the BZW unit fell 29 percent, was down 15p at 819-1/2.

Earlier Barclays' posted a 13 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 2.36 billion stg, including a 70 million stg one-off gain on disposals, compared with analyst forecasts mostly in a range between 2.33 billion stg and 2.45 billion.
By 1151 GMT Barclays was down 34-1/2p at 11.99-1/2 stg, having rallied from an initial 68-1/2p tumble.
